reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern exhibits a robust ~77-point periodic cycle characterized by a sharp, symmetric V-shaped trough followed by a slow, noisy recovery to baseline. Each cycle contains one dominant deep trough (robust standardized value ≈ -20 to -21) lasting ~10–12 points, with steep descent (~−1.5 to −2.0 per point) and slightly gentler ascent (~+0.8 to +1.2 per point). The baseline between troughs is near zero (median ≈ −0.05 to +0.17), with low-amplitude high-frequency noise (MAD ≈ 0.38–0.76) and negligible long-term trend (slope per point ∈ [−0.27, +0.06]). Peak morphology is flat-topped or gently undulating, never sharp; troughs are consistently narrow and deep without secondary minima. Amplitude (90th percentile range) is stable at ~20–21 units. Roughness (~0.127–0.169) and curvature (~0.126–0.252) increase slightly with window length due to inclusion of more cycles, not intrinsic change. Boundary truncation is minimal in candidates 1–3; candidate 0 ends mid-recovery, but its single-cycle shape matches the consensus. Acceptable variation includes minor shifts in baseline level (±0.2), slight asymmetry in trough slope, and small fluctuations in inter-trough noise—provided the core V-shape and depth remain intact.
